name: Elektra Records
editorial_article: Founded in 1950 by Jac Holzman in New York City, Elektra Records stands as one of the most significant and culturally influential independent labels in American music history. Starting as a boutique operation fueled by Holzman's passion for folk, ethnic music, and high-fidelity sound, Elektra famously grew from a small folk-centric enterprise—recording artists like Jean Ritchie and Theodore Bikel—into a formidable force in the 1960s rock and blues explosion. The label’s willingness to challenge conventions was evident early on, notably when Holzman defied the McCarthy-era blacklist to sign and record folk singer Josh White. \n\nBy the mid-1960s, Elektra transitioned into the rock era, with producers like Paul Rothchild helping to redefine the label’s sonic identity. This period saw the signing of seminal acts such as The Doors and the Paul Butterfield Blues Band, the latter being instrumental in legitimizing electric blues for a mainstream audience. Beyond its roster of iconic rock and singer-songwriter talent—which would grow to include Judy Collins, Carly Simon, and later, metal giants like Metallica—Elektra also innovated in business and design. The 1964 launch of its Nonesuch subsidiary, guided by the philosophy of providing "Quality Recordings at the Price of a Quality Paperback," revolutionized classical and avant-garde distribution. With its long-standing reputation for championing "icons and iconoclasts," Elektra remains a cornerstone of the recording industry, bridging the gap between underground authenticity and mainstream cultural impact across seven decades.

editorial_description: An influential independent label founded in 1950, Elektra evolved from a folk music pioneer to a powerhouse of rock, blues, and later alternative and metal, known for its commitment to high artistic standards and iconic roster.
